utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani. A few minutes ago you stated that you wanted to say something about what you were asked to recognise yesterday. Yesterday you were put clear questions to which you provided clear answers. How come you now wish to change what you have stated yesterday?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have given a statement earlier. Yesterday I wasn't feeling very well and my intention to clarify things today was just to actually clarify them, for things to be understood better. This is the aim, nothing else, because that part is not explained in details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Unless you're challenging it, Mr. Cepic, it doesn't seem to me it's a reasonable area for inquiry. But if you wish to challenge what was said yesterday, I would understand you doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, Your Honour. I was just surprised by his wish to change, having in mind the examination that went on yesterday. Thank you, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Shabani, my name is Branko Lukic. Together with Mr. Boris Zorko and Mr. Ogrizovic, I appear on behalf of General Lukic. I would like to start with the beginning of your testimony today when you said that you amended your statements. You said that on page 3, line 11 of today's transcript. You said you did that because another witness who testified together with you was not invited to testify in this proceeding. How did you learn of this fact, from whom?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was asked by members of the Tribunal, we were told that the village will be divided into two based on the river that runs through the village. So this was a point I wanted to make about certain incidents that occurred on the other side of the village. I was not allowed to speak of those incidents. I thought that another person would speak of those incidents, about the movements of the population in the other part of the -- Zhegra, which moved not in the same direction that we took in the direction of Presheva --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, my question must have been imprecise. I asked you from whom did you learn that this other person was not going to testify before this Tribunal? Could you please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that that person was also a witness for this Tribunal, but he was not called to testify. And if he was called, he would testify to those incidents that happened there, in that part of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Again, my question must have been imprecise. Please bear with me and maybe now I will finally succeed to pose the question right. Who did you learn from that that witness was not going to testify before this Tribunal? Please focus and try to answer my question.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The person himself from Zhegra told me this, that he was not called to testify.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you talked to other witnesses about this, as to whether you were going to testify here and what you were going to testify about, right?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not talk to the other person. I just asked: Are you going to testify or not? That's it. I didn't speak of anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you know what he was going to testify about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because he was of the other part of the village, and I assumed that he was going to be called to testify for the incidents that occurred in his part of the village. This is the reason. And whatever he would have said here, it would have only made the picture more complete about the events that happened in Zhegra.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani. So it is your assertion now that you had assumed that. Yet another one of your assumptions, right? That is not something that the man said to you actually.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't tell me anything, and I didn't even ask him about what he was going to testify. I only asked him: Why haven't you been invited? I don't know was his answer. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We were asked today to clarify matters with regard to uniforms and recognition. His Honour Judge Bonomy asked us to clarify the matter with you today if any one of us could deal with that. So I would like to embark on that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see P1326 now, please, with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're waiting for it to appear on our screens. Yesterday my learned friend Mr. Stamp, on page 2.689, line 19, asked you -- I'll read it in English so that you will get the right translation so I'll read the original. [In English] "You said that you saw soldiers in the vicinity of your village. Did you see any of the uniforms that they wore while they were there in that -- in that photograph?" [Interpretation] And the photograph that my learned friend showed you was precisely this one. On that photograph, there are uniforms worn by soldiers in your village, and you recognised 4, 6, and 9 as being photographs of that. What is it that you would like to explain to us?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to explain that uniform number 10, as well number 1 and number 5, were worn by the regular army, Serbian forces in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So can we conclude now in your opinion the uniforms that were worn by the army in your village are under numbers 1, 4, 5, 6, and 10, right?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: 4 and 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I think 4, 5, 6, 9 we had also yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. So now it includes 1, 4, 5, 6 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, 9 too.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And 9 too. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the Milosevic case on page 1.520, line 5, you said when Exhibit 18 was shown to you, which is actually identical to the one that we're viewing right now, you were asked: [In English] "Do you see any uniforms -- to what they were wearing in any of these paragraphs?" [Interpretation] You said: "Number 1." Then the Prosecutor asked you as follows: [In English] "Can you look and see whether you see any other uniforms before we put it on the overhead?" [Interpretation] And then you recognised a uniform, the one under number 2, actually, and number 9. What about today, do you recognise the uniform under number 2 as the uniform worn by the army?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't discern it very clearly because the picture is rather dark in my opinion. Yes, now this uniform I have also seen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to picture number 10. In picture number 10, if you take a closer look, you will see a KLA uniform. So in your village you saw these uniforms too, right?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that this uniform belonged to Serbian paramilitaries. This is what I meant, not to demonstrate that it was KLA uniform. Because at that moment I didn't see the insignia "KLA" on the arm. Had I seen it, I wouldn't have identified it as the Serb uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You do not see the left sleeve of this man where it says "KLA" -- "UCK" rather?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see it. That's why I'm saying that I thought that this uniform belonged to the Serb paramilitaries because I didn't see the insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, out of ten uniforms that were offered to you for recognition in terms of whether you saw them in your village or not, so far you've recognised seven as having been seen in your village, out of which one was a KLA uniform. Would you agree with me that you're not a reliable witness who can testify about what uniforms were in the critical period --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What uniforms appeared in your village in the critical period?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, that's not an appropriate way in which to formulate that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You may ask him if he's prepared to accept that his identification may not be reliable, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you accept, as put by His Honour Judge Bonomy, that identification of uniforms from the board here, the uniforms offered here, that your identification was not reliable?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not accept it. When I said that this is a Serb uniform, I didn't see the insignia. That's what I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you recognise not only insignia. You were recognising the pattern. Because on other uniforms, except for photographs 3 and 4, you did not identify or recognise any insignia, only the pattern. Would you agree, either -- either that this exhibit is not clear or is there another reason maybe for the fact that you did not properly identify the uniforms of the Serb forces in your village?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I was able to identify the Serb uniforms I've seen in my village, but as to this photo that we are discussing now, this reminds me of a Serb paramilitary who together with his captain were wearing the same uniform. That's why I said -- similar --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Shabani, all of these camouflage uniforms are similar. You were asked to identify exactly what uniforms were worn by the Serb forces in your village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have to say that that's not how I heard the question yesterday nor how I understood the approach, because that would be pretty ridiculous, would it not?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour. Very well. I shall conclude on this note. Actually, I would just like to put a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I thought my friend was about to move on. I just wanted to indicate for the record that when he spoke just now about uniforms 10 and 2, the photograph was expanded to cover the full screen, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Lukic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you something. Do you recall that at the trial of the late Slobodan Milosevic you identified uniforms under numbers 4, 6, and 9?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you asked a question earlier saying that he identified 1, 2, and 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1, 2, and 9. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you can understand the man's confusion now, can you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I beg your pardon. I shall repeat my question. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the trial of the late Slobodan Milosevic you identified only uniforms under numbers 1, 2, and 9?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe at that time it was as you are saying. But now that I look at these pictures I can recognise Serb forces uniforms, 3, 6, and the ones I already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we are getting yet another number. Now we have number 3 as well. So right now from this photograph you recognised eight uniforms that appeared in your village in the critical period, although at the trial of the late Slobodan Milosevic you were asked: [In English] "Can you look and see whether you see any other uniform?" "Any other uniforms ..." [Interpretation] At that moment you did not recognise any other uniform except for the uniforms under numbers 1, 2, and 9 respectively. Today you identified yet another five uniforms. Is that the explanation that you sought from this Trial Chamber? Is that for what you asked permission to explain?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My purpose was to stress -- to point out also the uniforms worn by the paramilitaries; that was my intention.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, to conclude, in the Milosevic case you recognised the uniforms that were worn by soldiers under numbers 1, 2, and 9, and today as you uniforms worn by the paramilitaries you marked numbers 3, 4, 5, 6, and 10. Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I'm not very certain of number 10. I think this is a uniform -- now I see it's uniform worn by the KLA soldiers. But similar to it I saw Serb paramilitaries wearing the similar uniforms without the insignia, KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani. We have dealt with this topic. If further clarification is required, the Prosecutor can deal with it during his re-direct perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the registrar to place on the screens Exhibits -- Defence Exhibits D -- sorry, 6D69. [In English] And since this document is in B/C/S, we provided partial, unofficial translation for Your Honours, the Prosecutor, and these partial translations have already been delivered to the booths. I was just reminded that we have to make one correction, housekeeping matter, because yesterday we said that that statement of Mr. Dren Caka should have been 6D69, but now it would be 6D71, because of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because we have 70 as well after this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So 6D69 from yesterday's cross-examination is 6D71?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this one, like any other which is untranslated into English --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: As a -- so far as it's an exhibit in the trial. And it's for you to produce the official translation of what's relevant when the position will be reviewed by the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Shabani, my learned friend Mr. Ackerman asked you whether you knew about certain criminal proceedings that had been initiated against certain persons for the killings that were committed in the village of Zegra. You have before you -- at least we hope that soon it will be before you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is this anything to do with the proceedings that Mr. Ackerman asked about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But the witness has denied any knowledge of these.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to confirm the names of killed persons in this document, so later on we can be sure that the document is dealing with the same killings as we have in his statement. I'm not asking him about the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The ones Mr. Ackerman put he told us were not in his statement, I think. You're putting something that you say is covered in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Actually, no. It's a new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The new statement is not in the evidence, right, the latest one from the 2006?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, it is in the evidence. You say it's the names referred to in it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the new one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, where are the translations that you say are available for -- oh, sorry, I have got it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The new statement given by this witness in -- on 27th of August, 2006, is the evidence, then we can find names from this document -- actually from this case in paragraph 7, paragraph 11 and 12.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, paragraph -- this is in the new statement, paragraphs --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's your question, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you. On the page 6 of this document and on the page of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following names are being mentioned, the names of the persons who were killed, and seven persons were charged for that crime, as you can see from this document. [In English] On the first paragraph, on the page 7 says: "During the time-period from 29th of March until 31st of March, 1991 [sic], in village of Zhegra, in Gjilan municipality, the following persons have been murdered by fire-arms and knife." And then we have those names which I would like this witness to confirm that correspond to the names from his statement. And the names are: "Ukshin Ukshini and his wife Ukshin Xhevahire. Haziri Qazim and his wife Haziri Qamile, Idrizi Milazim, and Tahiri Shyqri."

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milazim Idrizi and Shyqri Tahiri.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's the first paragraph on top of this page. And it's exactly the first paragraph, and we have three last lines are lines with the names, although it's in Cyrillic so I don't know how this witness is familiar with Cyrillic. But ...

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know how to read, but it's not clear, the handwriting is not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we not -- I don't know why we need this document. Why can't you simply ask him to confirm the names of people he knows were killed and then you can relate the document to his statement later. But why do we need to have them all out here and try to work through paper and make the thing complicated when it could be simplified?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Shaqiri [sic], did you mention in your statement as having been killed the following persons: Ukshini Ukshin, was he killed?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I have mentioned that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: His wife Ukshini Xhevahire?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Her name is not Xhevahire. I think it's different.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Haziri Qazim? Did you mention him as being killed?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Qazim Haziri, yes, I know him. He's a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Idrizi Milazim?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's the brother of Qazim Haziri.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And Tahiri Shyqri?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shyqri Tahiri, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Shabani, yesterday before we got your amended statement, I had not had any questions for you; regrettably, now that we have a new statement, we will have to go through some of its parts that I'm interested in as well. In your statement dated the 13th of June, 2001, in six different places you mention paramilitary forces. If you wish, we can move paragraph by paragraph. For example, page 2, paragraph 5; Albanian page 2, paragraph 5; B/C/S paragraph 2 -- paragraph 5, rather, on page 2. Whenever you mention paramilitary forces, in this statement from 2001 you never said that the police forces were with them or anyone from the police for that matter. Do you want us to deal with this paragraph by paragraph or will you accept that not anywhere in your paragraph [as interpreted] of 2001 did you mention the police in the presence of the paramilitary forces?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my statement I said military and paramilitary forces. By military forces I mean the regular army and the regular police and the reservist police and the reservist army forces. By paramilitary forces, I mean those forces who have another image in our eyes, who have other identification marks or signs. For me, these are the paramilitary forces. Every time I have used "paramilitaries," I've also said "military forces."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. When you talk about paramilitaries [as interpreted], all you mention is soldiers, not policemen. And you say those were members of the regular forces of the VJ. When you say these were regular VJ forces, do you include the police in that as well?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything that was commanded by higher ranks and worked in a hierarchy I called military forces. So their hierarchy is vertical, from above below, and this implies both the police and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Does that include the border-line as well? For example, in paragraph in English page 5, paragraph 4; in Albanian, paragraph 2, page 5; in B/C/S, page 5, paragraph 2. Were the police there as well as the soldiers and paramilitaries and reserve army forces and reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were police reservists, army reservists, that is soldiers, older in age but dressed in military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, on the border, in your view and as you put it today, there were reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also they could have been soldiers, both regular and reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you don't make any distinction between the two?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The distinction I make is on the basis of the uniforms they wore on the way how they appeared in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one correction, as I can see, page 58, line 18, my question was: "When you talk about military, all you mention is soldiers, not policemen." And in the transcript I can see that it says: "When you talk about paramilitaries," but I didn't ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we note that, but in any event the answer is contained earlier, isn't it? And that question really was a repetition.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your village there was a police station. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many policemen served in that police station, if you know?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number of policemen who served there. This police station covered a wider region, more villages, not only Zhegra. And to tell you the truth, I don't know how many were there. And it was not something that I showed interest in learning. They moved a lot. They changed their residence a lot, and that's why I don't know the exact number. However, during the war, their number multiplied.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you still give us an approximation of how many people there were in your police station in your village?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. Maybe 10 to 20 regular policemen, even 30. Really, I can't tell you the exact number because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you talk about those people you indeed say "policemen." And based on your previous answer, one would think that you cannot distinguish between a policeman, a soldier, and a paramilitary?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I object to this statement. It is not a question. I think the evidence should just be elicited by questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will rephrase, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you talk about policemen in your statement from your village, the policemen from your village, does that mean that you were able to recognise or distinguish their -- between their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were different. They wore different uniforms from others.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So when you talk about other forces with them or close to them, there were no people wearing the same type of clothing as was worn by the policemen of your village?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you referring to? I don't understand your question. If you could rephrase it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Certainly. Is it correct that when you talk about policemen and their movements, you described them as such in your statement since you were able to recognise their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have mentioned policemen in my statement as well as distinguished by me as such, not only as part of Serb forces but as policemen specifically. And I've mentioned this on two or three places in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. Thank you, Mr. Shabani. In your village you said there was also the TO; you mentioned that in paragraph 5 of your latest statement. What about their uniform? Is it one of the eight uniforms you recognised today or do they have something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we get the paragraph where he refers to the TO?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 5, paragraph number 5, "the commander of Territorial Defence in Zegra, Mikan, son of Slobodan."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not Mikan. It's Stavre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can certainly make that correction, but this is what we received from the Prosecutor, at least that's how this paragraph reads.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for Mikan, he was part of the reservist police.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned a reserve policeman, do you know of Cvetko Petrovic, have you heard of such a name? He was supposed to have been from your village.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard this name. Before the war I have seen this person, but not later.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Cvetko Petrovic on the 7th of May, 1999, was arrested because of theft and arson in the village of Zegra?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know this detail. You know better than me about the works of the police and the army. Personally, I don't know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know why you think I'm a military or police expert, but thank you in any case.

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not you in person, but your clients, those that you represent, those that are being tried here before this Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may have a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to go back again, and this will perhaps conclude my examination, to go back to uniforms. Today, out of ten uniforms you recognised eight. In the Milosevic trial, you said that you could recognise paramilitaries only by wearing Balaclavas --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Bandannas.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we, with your permission, have the transcript reference for that where he said only by wearing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the page 1556 in Milosevic trial when asked: "What you mean by 'paramilitary'?" And on line 23: "How can you differentiate between the paramilitary and the army?" The witness said: "I can differentiate between them in the way they were dressed. The paramilitary wear -- used some handkerchiefs."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the only difference in your view between the army and the paramilitary. Is that correct or do you believe that there are some other differences as well? And then we may go into those differences in terms of uniform. [Realtime transcript read in error: "A" omitted].

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only the bandannas, masks, cockades with the four S's. So these are the paramilitary forces. They were also wearing camouflage uniforms, but their uniforms differed from the uniforms of the military forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many types of uniform were there in your village, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The uniform of the regular police, the uniform of the regular army --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I may have been insufficiently clear. You described the paramilitaries by having said that some had cockades, masks, bandannas. How many different types of paramilitary uniform were there in your village?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two or three types, those that I've already mentioned, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Plus the eight you recognise gives us a sum total of over 11 types of uniform in your village alone. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought we had established that three of the eight were paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that the uniform in the picture number 10 belonged to the paramilitary. Is this what the other uniforms looked like?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In fact, just for the avoidance of this, that's my mistake. There actually were four plus number 10 that were paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand your question, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We've dealt with the problem of paramilitaries with the assistance of His Honour Lord Bonomy. He reminded me that you mentioned that among the eight you recognised. What about the TO, did they have their own uniform?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had almost the same uniform as the regular army, only that they were older in age.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one housekeeping matter again. It's page 63, line 6, the answer starts with: "Not only" and should -- this way it looks like it's part of the question. From the fourth line, "not only" is the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. That's noted. Thank you. Now, is that you complete, Mr. Lukic, or have you more?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have any more questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Shabani, for having answered my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will have one question to clarify something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We'll have that question after our break. Do you have questions, Mr. -- is there much re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. Sorry. No, not much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we'll resume, in fact, in 20 minutes, just after 25 to 1.00, and as I did indicate we'll finish early. We may even finish around quarter past, somewhere between quarter past and half past, the outside, but preferably nearer quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, actually, I'd like to clarify a particular matter so we will move very fast. It has to do with the witness statement related to the military man, Dusan. First the witness said that he saw him, and then in the corrected version, paragraph 6 that we got from the Prosecution, he said that he heard about that from yet another person. So my question is as follows: Did he hear about it from the person who had actually seen it or did that person hear about it from yet another person? It pertains to the incident that is referred to in the witness statement as the witness having seen it personally. Would that policeman Dragan, that they saw a man killed, and then later on he corrected that. In the interview on the 27th of August, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you say that's in paragraph 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, paragraph 6, paragraph 6. Was it paragraph 6? Paragraph 6, yes, of the additional statement. And it's paragraph 4 of the first statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I certainly am clearly of the view that he heard of this from someone else, and that applies to the whole incident. If that helps --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I thought, too. But then this other person that he heard it from, did that person see it with his very own eyes or did he hear about it from yet another person? That's my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you understand that question, Mr. Shabani? You were telling us about the killing of Avni, and you told us that you heard about that two days before the air-strikes ended, and you told us that you had heard about it from -- sorry, it happened two days before the air-strikes ended and you heard about this after you returned. Did the person who told you actually see it happen himself or had he heard it from someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This person witnessed it because they were together with Avni up until the village, then they parted their ways. Each went home. And at that moment when he heard shots, that Avni was killed, this is how he told me the entire event. Hisen Hiseni. Because as I said from Rimnik they travelled together with Avni to Zhegra.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What we're trying to find out is how much the person who told you actually saw. Now, he obviously, from what you've said, did not see the killing taking place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He only heard the shot. He heard that Avni was killed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What did he do after he heard the shot?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was nothing he could do. He went back to Rimnik where he was staying before he came to Zhegra, the person who recounted me this story I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that means he didn't even see the body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He couldn't see the body because the Serbs were firing. He saw it from the distance of his house because the Serbs were on a hill. Avni was walking towards his home. And when they shot at Avni, he, this person, saw him falling down on the ground. And he immediately left. He went back to -- to that village, Rimnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have anything else you wish to ask him, please ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'd just like to apologise to the witness. I haven't introduced myself. My name is Toma Fila, I'm an attorney-at-law, and I'm Defence counsel for Nikola Sainovic. Thank you no further questions

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. And we know that Mr. O'Sullivan has no questions. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know whether this is a confusion or what, but when Your Honour was talking about what he had said today about how he learned this, you mentioned that he learned about it after he returned and what he says in his most recent statement is he learned about it in Macedonia, before he returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Ackerman. As you could hear, I was not clear in my mind when I was asking that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm not sure --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I entirely accept that there are these two versions in the two statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm just not sure it was clear earlier, and I wanted to make sure that that was cleared up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said that you were told by Serbian forces that you should go to Presevo, which is in Serbia, but you did not go there. You deviated and went to Macedonia. Why did you not go to Presevo?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there were other Serbian forces deployed there, and we were scared of them. We were afraid we would suffer in their hands. Because we knew that they wouldn't have helped us because they had never helped any of the groups that went in that direction. That's why we went in the direction of Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You say that they had never helped any of the groups that went in that direction. How did you become aware of this? How did you become aware of the groups that went in that direction were treated?

utterances.speaker: QAMIL SHABANI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the group that came after us and to -- travelled almost the same route that we did, the son of my brother was with that group and they told us their hands were tied behind their backs, all the males. And they were beaten and subjected to all forms of mistreatment. And then they were put on some trucks after that, closed trucks, and were sent to Blace, from Gjilan to Blace. And I saw my nephew come there after four or five days to Macedonia. That's why I'm saying that. People were mistreated, seriously mistreated, and that's why we didn't go there. The same fate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The trouble with that explanation is that you learned from your cousin -- your nephew after you got to Macedonia, and I think that Mr. Stamp wanted to know about events that you were aware of before you went to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we went to Macedonia, we learned of what the other groups had gone through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You're not understanding my question. What -- what Mr. Stamp --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what Mr. Stamp wants to know is what you knew about things that had happened to other groups before you yourselves went to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We heard of this mistreatment. We heard that groups that went to Macedonia -- on the route to Macedonia were caught by the Serbian forces and maltreated. We heard of these events when we were there. That's why we were afraid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you were where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We were still in Stublla without setting out for Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Shabani, that completes your evidence. Thank you for coming again to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, who has the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next witness we intend to call is Abdylhaqim Shaqiri from Gjilan, or Gnjilane. He will testify about deportations, and his testimony relates to 72(i) and 73 of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is he a via any form of statement or is he a --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He is a viva voce witness, Your Honour. We had estimated his direct testimony at two to two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, we won't get very far with the evidence, Mr. Hannis, but we can have him sworn and you can start, if that's what you wish to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no particular preference. In some ways, it might be advantageous to me to not start with him since we are not resuming again until Tuesday. If there's some detail I want to talk to him about before then, I could do it if he's not sworn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't see anybody leaping to their feet to oppose that suggestion. This time the time lost will be held against the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour. Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think in the circumstances you're probably right, that the best decision is to hear the witness on Tuesday, but I raised it with you because if you were anxious to give him the opportunity to be in court and see the start of the proceedings, then you would have been free to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we will sit again on Tuesday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we sit Tuesday to Thursday next week in the morning -- in the afternoon and sit on Friday morning again. We're doing quite well on the Friday mornings so far. I think the week after that will also be a Friday morning. So we'll now adjourn until Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 5th day of September, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.
